title: WPSB/412/2014 of Devendra Singh Vs Uttarakhand Public Service Commission AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (SB) No. 412 of 2014
Devendra Singh. ..... Petitioner.
Versus
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
and ors. ..... Respondents.
Mr. Manoj Tewari, Sr. Advocate with Ms. Swati Verma, Advocate for the petitioner,
Mr. BD Kandpal, Advocate for UPSC/respondent no.1.
Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel for the State/respondent no.2.
Dated: April 22, 2015
Coram :Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
V.K. Bist, J. (Oral):
 The State Legislature has enacted the U.P.
Public Services (Reservation for Physically Handicapped,
Dependents of Freedom Fighters and Ex-Servicemen) Act,
1993, which is still applicable in the State of Uttarakhand.
According to the said legislation, in public services and
posts, 2% of vacancies shall be reserved at the stage of
direct recruitment for dependents of freedom fighters. On
03.03.2012, the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
(hereinafter referred to as the Commission) issued an
advertisement, by which 60 vacancies for the post of
Forest Range Officer were advertised. In the said
advertisement, it was mentioned that the dependents of
freedom fighters shall be entitled to reservation to the
extent of 2% in terms of the Government Order dated
18.07.2001 and Notification dated 07.11.2002. Similarly,
10% posts were reserved for 'Rajya Andolankaris' (State
Agitators, who agitated for creation of State of
Uttarakhand). The petitioner responded to the said
advertisement and claimed benefit of reservation in the
category of dependents of freedom fighters. He was issued
Admit-Card; he appeared in the preliminary examination;

2
and was declared successful. On 5th May, 2014, the result
of the main examination was declared, in which the
petitioner was declared successful. On 10.07.2014, final
result of selection was published, in which, no one
belonging to the category of dependent of freedom
fighters was declared successful. However, in the note, it
was mentioned that selection shall be subject to the final
outcome of Writ Petition (S/B) No. 330 of 2013.
Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application under the
Right to Information Act before the Commission. The
petitioner was informed by the Commission about the
interim order dated 20th March, 2014 passed in Writ
Petition (SB) No. 330 of 2013. In that writ petition, the
following interim order was passed:-
".......Prima-facie, it appears that the
reservation of vacancies in favour of
dependents of freedom fighters, as
provided in The Uttar Pradesh Public
Services (Reservation for Physically
Handicapped, Dependents of Freedom
Fighters and Ex-Servicemen) Act, 1993,
is contrary to the provisions of Article 16
of the Constitution of India.
Accordingly, we stay such reservation in
matters relating to employment or
appointment to any office under the
State."
2. Due to the above interim order, the
Commission did not consider the candidature of the
petitioner for selection under the category of 'dependents
of freedom fighters'. The result of Forest Range Officers
was declared on 10th July, 2014. In the said result, the
vacancy, which was earmarked for the candidates under
the category 'dependents of Freedom Fighters', was
treated as for general category candidates. Later on, on
26th September, 2014, the Writ Petition (S/B) No. 330 of

3
2013 was dismissed as withdrawn. Consequently, the
interim order stood vacated. Another writ petition was
also filed, titled as Writ Petition (PIL) No. 67 of 2011, in
which also similar interim order was passed on 26th
August, 2013, regarding posts relating to Rajya
Andolankaries. That interim order is still continuing.
3. The State Government, in regard to the
candidates belonging to the category of 'Rajya
Andolankaris', issued a communication to the
Commission on 23rd December, 2014 for keeping the said
post unfilled, but in respect of the dependents of Freedom
Fighters, such communication was not sent. The
Commission acted on the basis of the advice of the State
Government and kept four posts vacant, which were
earmarked for 'Rajya Andolankaris', but in regard to the
candidates belonging to dependents of freedom fighters,
the Commission filled up the post from general category
candidates. When the petitioner's candidature was not
considered under the category of dependents of Freedom
Fighters, the present writ petition has been filed. In the
case in hand, pleadings have been exchanged.
4. The contention of learned Senior Advocate for
the petitioner is that the petitioner was not at fault at any
point of time. It is also contended that the Act, which
provides reservation for the dependents of Freedom
Fighters is still operative and only for a short period, the
said provision was stayed by the High Court. He further
contends that in any case, the interim order merged in the
final order and in the case in hand, when the Writ Petition
(SB) No. 330 of 2013 was dismissed on 26.09.2014, the
Commission should have recommended the name of the

4
petitioner for selection under the category of dependents
of Freedom Fighters. He vehemently contends that the
interim order cannot determine the fate of the petitioner
candidates.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the
Commission submits that the Commission also was not at
fault, as at the relevant time when the result was declared,
the interim order was in operation and after the
declaration of the result only, the writ petition was
dismissed. He also submits that by that time, the
Commission recommended the names of the candidates
and the names were also sent to the State Government.
He submits that the candidature of the petitioner was also
considered under general category candidate, but since he
scored less marks, he was not recommended. If the
candidature of the petitioner had been considered by the
Commission under the category of 'dependents of
Freedom Fighters', then the Commission, in that event,
would have committed contempt of this Court's order
dated 20.03.2014 passed in Writ Petition (SB) No. 330 of
2013.
6. Shri Pradeep Joshi, learned Standing Counsel
for the State also submits that in fact, after
recommendation was received by the State Government,
appointment letters were sent to all the candidates; out of
which, 49 joined, one refused to join and 6 sought
extension. Thus, it is clear that out of 56 posts, one post is
still vacant.
7. Learned counsel for the Commission would
also submit that the name of the petitioner can not be

5
considered at this stage in view of the Government Order
of 2006, which provides that after selection, in case some
person does not join, the said vacancies shall be carried
forward, if there is no provision already exist in the
relevant service rules.
8. We have carefully considered the submissions
of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned
counsel for the respondents. In our considered view, in
the present case, the petitioner cannot be blamed, at all;
he applied for the advertised post under the reserved
category earmarked for the 'dependents of Freedom
Fighters', and his name was to be considered by the
Commission under that category. But due to interim order
passed by this Court in Writ Petition (SB) No. 330 of
2013, he was not considered under that category. It would
have been proper for the Commission to keep 2% posts
vacant till the disposal of Writ Petition (SB) No. 330 of
2013. Once that petition was dismissed, the law relating to
reservation for dependents of Freedom Fighters shall be
treated as valid law, even for that period also when
interim order was in operation. In our view, the petitioner
is entitled to be considered against the 2% posts
earmarked for dependents of Freedom Fighters.
9. We are surprised that the State Government
has written to the Commission to keep vacant only those
posts which were reserved for 'Rajya Andolankaris', but
simultaneously, kept silent in the matter of the
dependents of Freedom Fighters. This action of the State
Government is not, at all, commendable. We think that
only due to inaction on the part of the State Government,
the petitioner has suffered. As far as the contention of the

6
learned counsel for the Commission that the post should
be carried forward is concerned, we have put this query to
the Standing Counsel for the State, who contends that in
case, an order is passed, the post earmarked for the
candidates falling under the category 'dependents of
Freedom Fighters' will not be carried forward. We find
that this Court vide interim order, has already directed to
keep one post vacant. In such circumstances, we think
that justice will be done to the petitioner, if a direction is
issued to the Commission to consider the candidature of
the petitioner under the category 'dependents of Freedom
Fighters' and if he is found to have obtained minimum cut
off marks in that category, and is up in the merit, his
name be recommended. We order accordingly.
10. Learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner
then submits that there is only one more candidate,
namely, Mr. Digambar Singh, and the petitioner has
scored more marks than the said candidate, who has
scored 50 marks less than the petitioner. This fact has not
been denied by the counsel for the Commission.
11. We also direct the State Government to take
immediate action in this regard, incase recommendation
is made by the Commission, but as per law.
12. This disposes of the writ petition. No order as
to costs.
(V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 22.04.2015
